transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Is there anything you'd like to ask me about?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, thanks for taking my call. I do have some questions about my recovery process. When can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for about a month, so keep the gardening gentle to start with.

Do you have any other questions about your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your care team.

If you don't have any left or are running out, your GP should be able to provide some more for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain when it's bright, or severe light sensitivity—especially if your eye is also red and painful—that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, please let your care team know.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I have one more question. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a common concern. It's quite normal to have some blurriness in the first week after surgery, and this should improve quickly and settle down over time.

However, if your vision is still blurry now or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay. How long has it been since your surgery?

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all the questions I have for now. Thank you so much for your help, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Before we finish, just to confirm—have all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been addressed. Thanks again for your assistance!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and best wishes with your recovery.
